title: Task definitions
idea: A task definition is the JSON blueprint ECS uses to start a task, one running copy of your containers. It names the image, ports, size and roles.
points: `family` names the blueprint; each registration adds a revision, such as `bookstore-api:2`.
Each entry in `containerDefinitions` sets one container's `image`, `portMappings` and environment.
On Fargate, set `networkMode` to `awsvpc` and pick a supported `cpu` and `memory` pair.
`executionRoleArn` lets ECS pull images and send logs. `taskRoleArn` is for your code.

code.title: Task definition
code.caption: The Book Store API as a Fargate task definition. `<account-id>` and `<region>` are placeholders.

walk.text: The family. Each registration under this name becomes the next revision.
ECS validates the definition for Fargate. Each Fargate task gets its own network interface.
The whole task: 256 CPU units and 512 MiB, one of the pairs Fargate accepts.
The role's ARN, its full AWS identifier. ECS uses it to pull the image and write logs.
The container: a name, and the ECR image address with a version tag.
`containerPort` is where the app listens. `PORT` tells the app which port to use.
`awslogs` sends the container's output to a CloudWatch Logs group. Create the group first.

code.title: Register it
code.caption: Register the file, then list the revisions. Each registration adds one.

walk.text: Send the JSON file to ECS. It replies with the new revision number.
List every revision in the family, such as `bookstore-api:1`.

pitfalls: Create the log group named in `awslogs-group` first; ECS does not create it by default.
Keep secrets out of `environment`; reference them with `secrets` instead.
Make `containerPort` equal the port your app listens on, the `PORT` value.

quiz.q: You register `bookstore-api` again with a new image tag. What happens to running tasks?
options: They restart on the new revision
They keep running the revision they started with
ECS rejects it: the family already exists
quiz.why: Registering only adds a revision, such as `bookstore-api:2`. Running tasks keep theirs; a service moves to the new revision when you update the service.

takeaway: Every `docker run` choice becomes a field, and every edit becomes a new revision.
